## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Dūtajātaka* (Ja 478), translated as *The Messenger*, is a birth story preserved in the Pali Jātaka collection [SuttaCentral]. According to the traditional introductory narrative, the Buddha recounted this story while dwelling at Jetavana in praise of his own wisdom, opening with the verse beginning "O plunged in thought" [SuttaCentral]. The narrative illustrates how the Buddha was skilled in means (*upāyakusala*) not only in his final life but also across his past births [Pye; Fausböll 1887]. Michael Pye observes that the text specifically highlights this theme and includes an incidental reference to the training of Nanda in the *Nandajātaka* (Ja 182) as an instance of *upāya* [Pye]. In the commentary's identification of the birth (*samodhāna*), the Bodhisatta is revealed to have been the young student (*māṇava*), while Ānanda was the king and Sāriputta was the teacher [Fausböll 1887].

Textual reuse analyses show nine shared passages between the canonical verses and the fourth volume of the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. While SuttaCentral records no curated cross-linguistic parallels [SuttaCentral], DharmaNexus identifies automated text-reuse matches between this Jātaka and Sanskrit literature, most notably the *Kāraṇḍavyūha Sūtra*, alongside minor alignments with the Tibetan translation of the *Jātakamālā* [DharmaNexus].
